stories.title: First human trial of a B7-H4 drug conjugate shows tumour responses
stories.summary: The Phase 1/2a BLUESTAR study of AZD8205, or puxitatug samrotecan, reported partial tumour responses in previously treated patients with advanced ovarian, endometrial and breast cancer. It enrolled 47 patients with B7-H4-positive solid tumours, and results were published in Nature Communications.

stories.title: Hospital patients treated by female physicians fared better, Ontario study finds
stories.summary: Patients treated in hospital by female physicians were less likely to die or be readmitted than those treated by male physicians, according to a University of Toronto and ICES study in JAMA Network Open. The authors describe it as an association among patients with common medical diagnoses.

stories.title: Untrained dogs may detect a stranger's seizure by scent
stories.summary: University of Milan researchers presented sweat samples from a six-year-old girl with epilepsy, taken during and outside seizures, to 30 dogs unfamiliar with her, ScienceAlert reports. The study suggests even untrained dogs with no detection experience may pick out seizure samples.

stories.title: Retatrutide reduced sleep apnoea symptoms in a trial
stories.summary: A study in people with overweight or obesity found that the experimental weight-loss drug retatrutide greatly reduced obstructive sleep apnoea symptoms, Medical News Today reports. The condition pauses breathing during sleep and is often undiagnosed, so there are no definitive figures on how common it is.

stories.title: FDA approves NRx's preservative-free ketamine injection
stories.summary: The US FDA has approved NRx Pharmaceuticals' abbreviated new drug application for preservative-free ketamine injection, its first approved product, ahead of a 10 November goal date. CEO Jonathan Javitt said approval came in under 14 months, against an average of 35.6 months cited from FDA data.

stories.title: Yale investigator explains the hope around the personalised melanoma vaccine
stories.summary: Dr Thuy Tran, Yale site principal investigator for the Phase 2 and 3 trials of Moderna and Merck's personalised melanoma vaccine, told the Hartford Courant it is 'the first cancer vaccine that's proven efficacy in advanced Phase 3 clinical trials'. Melanoma kills more than 8,000 Americans a year.

stories.title: A swab test may spare some women an endometrial biopsy
stories.summary: Researchers report that a simple vaginal swab may one day help women with abnormal bleeding learn whether they have endometrial cancer without first going through a painful biopsy, Medical Xpress reports. The full article was not accessible.

stories.title: Abemaciclib can raise creatinine without kidney damage, study finds
stories.summary: Researchers from Kanazawa University and Shinshu University found that the breast cancer drug abemaciclib often raises creatinine in a way that makes kidneys look like they are failing when they are not, Medical Xpress reports. A baseline measurement can help doctors tell the difference.

stories.title: University of Chicago team targets radiation's immune side effect
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Chicago have identified a mechanism to make immune cells reprogrammed by radiation therapy attack tumours rather than protect them, in a study in Cancer Cell, Medical Xpress reports. Radiation activates a protein called TET2 on immune cells in bone marrow.

stories.title: A ten-marker blood score aims to track healthy ageing
stories.summary: European researchers have created a personalised indicator using ten blood markers to flag disease risk and assess healthy ageing, Medical Xpress reports. Studies suggest about 60% of people over 65 live with two or more chronic conditions, which the work hopes to address.

stories.title: Hepatitis E vaccine well tolerated in women of childbearing age
stories.summary: An observational study in Karachi found the hepatitis E vaccine Hecolin safe and well tolerated among 375 non-pregnant women of childbearing age, with only mild, transient side effects over 21 days of follow-up. It was published in the Egyptian Liver Journal.

stories.title: India's Patent Office rejects a patent on the BPaL TB regimen
stories.summary: India's Patent Office has rejected a TB Alliance patent application covering the BPaL regimen of bedaquiline, pretomanid and linezolid for drug-resistant tuberculosis, in a decision issued on 27 October. It followed pre-grant oppositions filed in July 2020. Access advocates see it as a win for affordable medicines.

stories.title: India bars imports of drugs with under a year of shelf life
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has amended Rule 31 of the Drugs Rules, 1945, to bar imports of drugs with less than one year of residual shelf life on the import date, Medical Dialogues reports. Biologicals and radiopharmaceuticals may be imported with 60% of their labelled shelf life left.

stories.title: India reports 86.97 crore screenings for three common cancers
stories.summary: India has screened 86.97 crore people for oral, breast and cervical cancers, and about 5.50 lakh patients are being treated for them, Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava said at a Department of Posts event releasing breast cancer awareness stamps on Friday.

stories.title: Assam signs for India's first public proton beam therapy centre
stories.summary: Assam has signed an MoU with Belgium-based IBA for a proton beam therapy machine at Guwahati Medical College and Hospital, the first in India's public health system, Pratidin Time reports. It is estimated to cost Rs 600 crore and should be installed within three years.

stories.title: ICMR funds a four-year study of autoimmune disease in families
stories.summary: ICMR has funded a four-year study of the genetic and immune mechanisms behind autoimmune diseases in families with several affected members, led by Dr Dipyaman Ganguly of Ashoka University and Dr Ranjan Gupta of AIIMS Delhi. Doctors are asking SLE patients to enrol.

stories.title: Karnataka pauses its hospital medicine price disclosure rule
stories.summary: The Karnataka government told the High Court it will not enforce, until further orders, a 1 October circular requiring hospitals to show procurement price, MRP and price charged for medicines and devices in itemised bills from 1 November. A petition challenges the circular.

stories.title: Experts say India's stroke fight must target tobacco dependence
stories.summary: Experts on the eve of World Stroke Day called for sustained tobacco cessation support alongside blood pressure control, DT Next reports. A 2024 analysis of Global Burden of Disease data estimated tobacco contributed to 12% of stroke deaths in India and high systolic blood pressure to 56%.

stories.title: How gender shapes access to eye care in India
stories.summary: Women face disadvantages in access to eye care from childhood to old age, The Hindu reports, with treatment often depending on how men in the household prioritise their health. Late or missing care can leave girls and women with preventable visual impairment.

stories.title: Infant deaths in Attappady point to a deeper health crisis
stories.summary: Twelve infants, 10 of them from tribal communities, have died in Attappady in Kerala this year, and the state has ordered an expert probe, The Hindu reports. Activists say anaemia, malnutrition and low birth weight need action beyond healthcare.

stories.title: AIIMS Bhopal doctors train on robotic and digital surgical planning
stories.summary: AIIMS Bhopal specialists from surgical oncology, dentistry, plastic surgery and radiation oncology trained in simulation-based robotic surgery and virtual planning for jaw reconstruction during a two-day continuing medical education programme, the Times of India reports. Sessions focused on complex procedures and post-cancer reconstruction.

stories.title: Ebola deaths in DR Congo pass 5,000
stories.summary: More than 5,000 people have died in DR Congo's Ebola outbreak, the country's deadliest, with over 10,300 confirmed cases across eight of 26 provinces, the BBC reports. The case fatality rate is 48.6%. Cases have also been confirmed in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

stories.title: First Ebola vaccine trial doses given in DR Congo
stories.summary: The first dose of a trial vaccine against the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which is driving the current outbreak, was given in DR Congo this week, NPR reports. There is no approved vaccine or treatment for that species. WHO's Dr Meg Doherty is there for the trial.

stories.title: Lancet Countdown calls climate change a global health emergency
stories.summary: The 2026 Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change, from 146 researchers at more than 100 institutions, says climate change must be treated as a global health emergency. It warns that health risks from extreme heat, drought and fossil fuel pollution are rising faster than responses.

stories.title: WHO sets out health priorities for COP31
stories.summary: WHO's briefing for COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, from 9 to 20 November, says an estimated 3.3 to 3.6 billion people live in contexts highly vulnerable to climate change. It calls for climate-resilient, low-carbon health systems and implementing the Belem Health Action Plan.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia suspends travel to Kenya over Ebola risk
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia has suspended travel by its citizens to Kenya, halted visas for travellers from Kenya and banned their entry over Ebola risks, the Saudi Gazette reports. Travellers who stayed in Kenya or other affected countries in the previous 21 days are also barred.

stories.title: Florida weighs dropping four school vaccine requirements
stories.summary: The Florida Department of Health held a hearing in October on removing Hib, chickenpox, pneumococcal and hepatitis B vaccines from school and childcare entry requirements. An epidemiologist writing in The Conversation notes these diseases caused millions of cases before vaccination.

stories.title: Wisconsin confirms a measles outbreak in Chippewa County
stories.summary: Chippewa County, Wisconsin, had 33 confirmed measles cases as of 30 October, and officials now call it an outbreak with local spread, WEAU reports. A separate outbreak in southwest Wisconsin has 336 confirmed cases.

stories.title: Some Albany Med babies may need a repeat Hep B vaccine dose
stories.summary: New York's health department says some babies at Albany Medical Center may have received Hep B vaccines stored below the recommended temperature. It says there is no immediate danger but recommends another dose. Affected families have been notified, WRGB reports.

stories.title: UK experts say online misogyny should be treated as a public health issue
stories.summary: Authors of a report in the Lancet say the manosphere and online misogyny should be handled as a public health issue, like obesity or smoking, the Guardian reports. They call for a coordinated response from governments, schools, health services and community groups.

stories.title: Docterz raises Rs 5 crore, mostly from doctors who use it
stories.summary: Mumbai healthtech Docterz has raised Rs 5 crore from about 35 investors, with close to Rs 3 crore from around 20 doctors already on its platform, Mint reports. Its clinic software supports more than 5,000 doctors. The customers are now also the cap table.

stories.title: Mulk Technology and OnClarity pitch an ABDM-ready AI hospital platform
stories.summary: Mulk Technology and US-based OnClarity USA have partnered on an AI-enabled digital hospital platform with 22 modules, compliant with the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission, signed in Dubai on 23 October. It layers OnClarity's patient experience tools on Mulk's hospital management system.

stories.title: Vietnam targets digital health records for everyone on VNeID by June 2027
stories.summary: Vietnam's health ministry, with the public security ministry, is tasked with integrating electronic health records into the VNeID system for the entire population before 30 June 2027, according to an official notice reported by VietNamNet.

stories.title: Greek, Portuguese and Finnish universities graduate 77 in digital health
stories.summary: Aristotle University of Thessaloniki will award degrees to the first 77 graduates of its joint master's in digital health management on 3 November. The ManagiDiTH programme is run with Iscte in Lisbon and Finland's Laurea University of Applied Sciences.

stories.title: Nigeria trains health records tutors on digital data systems
stories.summary: Nigeria's Records Officers Registration Council is training health information management tutors on the DHIS2 software at a two-day retreat in Abuja, Daily Trust reports. Its head, Babagana Mustapha, said graduates must be ready for growing digital technology in health care.

stories.title: Researchers publish a dataset of 25,419 psychedelic support conversations
stories.summary: The Fireside Database, published in Science Advances, draws on 25,419 psychedelic support interactions to give researchers and policymakers a view of psychedelic use and support outside clinical settings, Medical Xpress reports. The full article was not accessible.

stories.title: One dose of a psychedelic nasal spray eased hard-to-treat depression for eight weeks
stories.summary: A single dose of a synthetic mebufotenin nasal spray eased treatment-resistant depression within a day, with benefits up to eight weeks, in a trial published in JAMA, PsyPost reports. Most patients were ready to leave the clinic within two hours.

stories.title: Diet and exercise put over half of young adults' type 2 diabetes into remission
stories.summary: More than half of young adults with type 2 diabetes achieved remission after a closely supervised six-month diet and exercise programme, in a Canada and UK study in The Lancet Regional Health Americas. Participants lost an average of 8.4 kg, against 1.2 kg in comparison.

stories.title: Children of centenarians show lower health risks, study finds
stories.summary: Adults with at least one parent who lived to 100 had much lower risks of death, heart disease and high blood pressure than people whose parents died younger, a JAMA Network Open study of 2,319 such adults and 2,703 comparison participants found.

stories.title: Papers weigh what permanent daylight saving time means for sleep
stories.summary: A CMAJ policy analysis argues permanent standard time would better support winter sleep, mood and body rhythms than permanent daylight saving time, PsyPost reports. A large population review found clock changes carry a mix of harms and benefits.

stories.title: Daily vaping linked to poorer vascular function in young adults
stories.summary: Daily nicotine vaping was associated with reduced vascular function and lower cardiorespiratory fitness in young adults who had never smoked cigarettes, according to a Manchester Metropolitan University study in JAMA Cardiology reported by Medical Dialogues.

stories.title: Coffee, with or without caffeine, linked to gut and mood changes
stories.summary: A small University College Cork study found caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee were both linked to changes in gut microbes and some mood measures, with different effects on cognition. 'Coffee is more than just caffeine,' said Professor John Cryan. Decaf drinkers may claim partial credit.

stories.title: Nearly half of young remote workers say it makes them lonely
stories.summary: The Bupa Wellbeing Index found 47% of 18 to 24 year olds feel remote working causes loneliness, up from 42% in 2025. Across all adults the figure was 34%, and only 18% of those aged 55 and over said the same.

stories.title: Living alone may be riskier for younger adults than seniors
stories.summary: A new study suggests living alone raises the risk of death from many causes, particularly among adults aged 18 to 64, more than among older people, Medical Xpress reports. Loneliness has usually been studied as a risk for seniors. The full article was not accessible.

stories.title: About one in four reviewers quit a newer insomnia drug
stories.summary: Researchers from Rutgers and other universities analysed hundreds of online reviews of lemborexant and found about one in four reviewers stopped or planned to stop taking the prescription insomnia medication, Medical Xpress reports. The full article was not accessible.

stories.title: Not all antihistamines affect the brain equally
stories.summary: Some antihistamines can cause sleepiness, slow reactions and affect concentration, while others are much less likely to, Medical Xpress reports. Knowing the difference can help people choose an allergy treatment that will not interfere with daily life.

stories.title: How constant urban noise affects health
stories.summary: DD India looks at noise pollution as a growing public health concern in India's expanding cities, driven by traffic, construction, industry and crowded spaces. It asks what constant exposure through day and night does to residents who rarely find quiet.

research.title: Scientists discover a bacterial defense so strange they thought it was broken
research.summary: Scientists have discovered a bizarre bacterial defense system that works almost completely backward from anything seen before. Unlike typical bacterial immune systems that keep a deadly toxin under control until a virus attacks, this unusual mechanism waits until an infection begins before producing the DNA that switches on.

research.title: Scientists finally discover how a common gut bacterium can trigger colon cancer
research.summary: Scientists at Johns Hopkins have uncovered a crucial missing link between a common gut bacterium and colorectal cancer, solving a mystery that has puzzled researchers for nearly two decades. The bacterium, Bacteroides fragilis, produces a toxin that damages the colon’s protective lining, triggers chronic inflammation, and promotes tumor.
